extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners (national phase) / staff at the national patent office (CIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Quality standards and evaluative criteria for conducting national patent examination (search, examination, communication, prosecution and timeliness) consistent with Office Practice, Patent Act, Patent Rules, MOPOP, Exam Bulletins and Practice Notices. Intended to guide examiners in assessing applications and preparing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Practice definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Office Practice" is the administration of the requirements of the Patent Act and Patent Rules using the guidance of MOPOP, Exam Bulletins and Practice Notices and with consideration also given to particularly relevant Commissioner's Decisions and Jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overarching framework examiners must follow: statutory provisions (Patent Act/Rules), internal manuals (MOPOP), exam bulletins and practice notices, and applicable commissioner decisions and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter issues are appropriately addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter issues include: lack of statutory subject matter or utility (section 2 and subsection 27(8) of the Patent Act); inadequate description of the invention (subsection 27(3) of the Patent Act, section 56 of the Patent Rules); introduction of new subject matter (section 38.2 of the Patent Act); lack of unity (section 36 of the Patent Act, and section 88 of the Patent Rules); and lack of support for claims (section 60 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must identify and address statutory subject matter defects, utility, sufficiency of description, added/new matter, unity and claim support, citing the correct statutory authority in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and/or examination is reserved when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Search and/or examination may be reserved (completely or partially) when deficiencies in the specification make it impractical to issue a comprehensive report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations justifying reservation include: specification too insufficient/unclear to search; claims directed solely to non-statutory subject matter; claimed subject matter not supported by the specification as filed; missing sequence listing preventing search; lack of unity; introduction of new subject matter (new subject matter is not examined). When reservation is used, the extent and reason must be clearly stated in the examiner's report. In lack of unity cases, inform applicant to elect one group linked by a single general inventive concept and limit further examination to that election.

rubrics_metrics.name: A correct search strategy is adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: A correct search strategy, where a meaningful search can be carried out: identifies the inventive concept(s) underlying the claims; includes a first-to-file search of Canadian patent documents; makes effective use of available search results; includes a supplemental/top up or comprehensive search, as required; and pays regard to the amount of searching that is reasonable and practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: perform first-to-file searches in Canadian patent documents (including non-laid-open) to identify novelty and overlap issues, aiming to identify documents filed/published in five years prior to filing date; for PCT national phase, consider PCT search results and IPRP/IPER when available; conduct comprehensive searches when no PCT ISR and no adequate foreign family search results; otherwise a first-to-file search may suffice. Supplemental/top-up searches should be used when examiner knowledge suggests additional prior art likely exists. When performing searches, rely on sufficient breadth to identify documents relevant to novelty and inventive step, use appropriate search fields and methods prioritizing fields with highest probability of finding relevant documents, and document the search strategy in the search record according to office practice. Note: do not search claimed embodiments not properly supported by the specification as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, obviousness and double patenting are appropriately addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner has reasonable grounds to believe that the invention is anticipated or obvious: the most relevant prior art is listed in the references section of the examiner's report; a summary of the relevant teachings of the prior art is provided; each lack of novelty defect is identified under section 28.2 of the Patent Act; and each obviousness defect is identified under section 28.3 of the Patent Act. Double patenting issues must also be identified when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When search fails to reveal pertinent references, state that. Assess each claim against prior art, with emphasis on independent claims; level of detail for dependent claims may vary by number of claims, prosecution stage and nature of limitations. For double patenting: identify conterminous or obviousness double patenting defects if same invention is claimed in pending application and issued Canadian patent to same applicant; identify defects under section 44 if necessary. Where overlap exists between copending applications, warn applicant in the report and maintain warning while overlap exists; when one co-pending application becomes allowable/granted, mark the other as containing a double patenting defect. Note: if an issued patent or co-pending application can be cited as prior art under section 28.2 or 28.3, separate overlap/double patenting defect need not be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formalities are appropriately addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Application formality defects include: lack of clarity of the claims (e.g., subsection 27(4) of the Patent Act, subsection 62(1), sections 63, 61 and 51 of the Patent Rules); drawings not furnished or not clear; description formalities such as unidentified trademarks, incorrect page numbering, incorporations by reference and inadequate publication details; title not short and precise; abstract not a concise summary; sequence listing not in correct format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity matters do not extend to minor defects of grammar or spelling which do not lead to ambiguity (i.e., which would not give rise to a defect under subsection 27(4)). An examiner should not delay allowance merely to clean up trivial language defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution is expedient
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner has reasonable grounds to believe that an application complies with Office Practice, either as originally filed or after all defects have been satisfactorily addressed by the applicant, the examiner approves the application for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expediency requires: consideration of the most recent version of the application whenever conducting examination; observance of national examination process mappings; consideration of foreign prosecution; comprehensive examination except where examination is reserved; exercising good judgment in identifying defects and maintaining identifications; and proper record keeping. For private inventors, adapt prosecution to assist understanding of the amendment process to comply with Office Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defect identifications are maintained when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment has removed a defect, the defect will no longer be identified; when convincing argument shows identification is no longer warranted, it will be removed; when a client response fails to overcome an identified defect, the defect will continue to be identified; when examiner and applicant reach an impasse on compliance regarding identified defects a Final Action rejecting the application will be written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides continuity of prosecution: maintain identifications unless convincingly overcome or removed by amendment; persist defects across actions when not overcome; escalate to Final Action when impasse exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: New defects are identified after the first report, when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of new defects may arise after a first report for reasons such as: as a result of an amendment or submission made by the applicant; as a result of new prior art of which the examiner has become aware; as a result of reserved examination; and as a result of a defect that was inadvertently not identified in a previous report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must identify subsequent defects that arise due to applicant amendments, newly discovered prior art, reserved examinations being lifted, or inadvertent omission earlier; these should be clearly explained in subsequent reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: All defects are identified in a sufficiently informative manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient detail is always provided when identifying a defect so that the applicant can understand the defect and determine an appropriate response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: reference to correct authority basis (Patent Act, Patent Rules or jurisprudence); appropriate explanation, particularly for obviousness or lack of clarity; indicate relevant passages of the application and prior art when appropriate; identify defective claims; identify groups and rationale for lack of unity defects; at second or subsequent report stages, address applicant's amendments and arguments when defects continue. Note: explanation may include a suggestion of a remedy, but must not dictate any specific remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate requisitions are made
rubrics_metrics.description: Requisitions or notices are made when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include requisitions/notices under sections 76, 85, 86, 196(1) and 94 of the Patent Rules or under subsection 27(5.2) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of examiner's report is clear and content is accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Written communications include matters of form, where appropriate: all information is accurate including agent contact information, application number, owner, title, classification, applicant reference number, examiner name and examiner telephone number; the basis of the report is clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report should clearly identify: any reservations to search/examination; the unity group elected by the applicant; the applicant's latest amendment; the number of claims; requisitions (sections 85, 86 and 94) clearly identified by a bullet in headers; citations correctly identified with sufficient detail to retrieve the document; content presented in logical order; search record present and complete; and a report for a private inventor may be more detailed and written in plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview records are accurate and complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview records include, where appropriate: all information is accurate including the names of participants, date of the interview, application number and summary of discussion and/or agreement; the agreed upon due date is included when a voluntary amendment is to be submitted to overcome identified defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure interview summaries capture participants, date, application details, summary of discussion/agreements and any agreed deadlines for amendments so records support subsequent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: All communications are professional and geared toward providing service excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communications require: straightforward language; a polite approach; and a suitable response to all requests and inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be professional, clear and courteous; tailored for service excellence (plain language for private inventors when appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination is performed in a timely manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness requires the observance of the time limits specified in the Priorities of Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to prescribed time limits/priorities and ensure examination workflow meets timing expectations set by office priorities.
